I want to like this game, but the upgrade map is mostly an illusion of choice. The game is more of a min/max puzzle. You have to puzzle solve the correct upgrades to complete each challenge, which is the only way to get more upgrades. In the beginning there is a fair amount of choice in what towers and upgrades you can win with, but as you progress you will realize that you either need luck or nearly the exact correct choices to complete the run. This isn't an inherently negative way to add difficulty, but its not fun, at least not for me. I like picking towers and seeing which ones work better and which are worse, and some choices should and will fail. This game doesn't work that way. It's mostly a minimum threshold of upgrades, and then you can win. It doesn't feel like skill or choice. Once you beat the final level, you are allowed to complete additional challenges, but these are "thread the needle" challenges. At this point the only challenge is picking the correct combination of upgrades or you lose, which makes most upgrades useless. The skill wall switches to checking the correct boxes. You just need to figure out which upgrades to turn on or off to win. I would recommend this game to players who like to min/max with trial and error.

A strategic tower defense incremental game that i've seen make a name for itself on TikTok and on Steam, with a throrough upgrade tree and changing currencies all around which gives you an extra challenge for a better reward. Sadly it didn't give me a lot of motivation or satisfaction to really continue on with it more than I wish I could, having more negative notes than positive. [spoiler] Starts off as a nice simple tower defense with only one defense to get currency to buy upgrades and eventually beat the more difficult unique bosses, special build challenges and rewards for being extra fast. With 10 levels to get you more resources and new enemies. [/spoiler] The couple positive things I could give this game is that the idea is really unique and brought to the extend that I haven't seen before, also how you can hover over currencies to see what upgrades are still available to be bought in a crowded upgrade tree and even clicking to see what amount you've already spent instead of showing what you still have left. But in the end it's missing a satisfying click to me, the way you expect to click in your head while playing it giving you an addictive feeling to want to continue, and with the eerie atmosphere it gives you a feeling that it isn't made with love. The upgrade tree gave me more satisfaction than the game itself. Something that also feels like it wasn't made with love; the lack of defying textures makes it a very forgettable game once you either finish it or finish playing it, only the gameplay has a staying factor to me. Secondly, In games where it matters and where it can be a difference of winning or losing: critical chances, not a fan of them since it can heavily chance the outcome of finishing a level, but since it's not too hard of a pushback and still gives you the resources you've collected it's not that bad but I always like to see a better way of combatting luck. Furthermore, I think having extra slots to have a custom build loadout is great, but unnecessary if you call the game in your own words "short" and to 100% achievement hunt the game you will have to unlock every single upgrade either way. Making it less useful (as far as I see, having completed the last level) unless you are looking for the "Pivot" achievement without actually deleting your tree progress. In addiction to the upgrade tree, accidentally right clicking on an upgrade and removing an entire branch of the upgrade tree has annoyed me more than I could tell you since i'm very used to having right click be the way you move around in upgrade trees. But after all this, the creator is still having future plans to make the game better, add more levels and content which does show that they're doing it for the love of the game even if it feels eerie right now. TL/DR: You could try this game out, but don't be afraid to refund if it feels unmotivating before 2 hours, i've seen my friend buy this and quit the first hour.

终于终于终于终于终于终于全成就辣！OMG！ 刚发售的时候就看朋友买了感觉还不错就入手了，一直没什么时间.. 毕竟玩塔防游戏还是需要一点脑子的_(:з」∠)_ ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜💙💚💛🧡❤️ 游戏对全成就玩家还算比较友好，主要是分为：1】过关成就，2】天赋点亮成就 虽然游戏只有10关（其实最后一关只是一个模式，其实也只是9关） 需要完成各种模式，全部打完就能全成就！还是比较友好的~ ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜💙💚💛🧡❤️ 游戏就是蛮中规中矩的塔防游戏，我们在天赋里可以解锁5种塔的类型~ 当然也有平A暴击，减速，中毒，点燃等等的效果！ 有多种模式的有9关，难度都是逐渐递增！ 普通模式就是中规中矩的，前期会卡关可以返回去玩一下其他模式。 一关除普通还有两个带限制条件的，奖励不同！ 天赋点升级卡的很死，必须要完成一些固定限制模式才能解锁！ 但是只要打到第10关，就可以算通关了，通关以后又会解锁代币模式和声望模式~ 也是类似给你限制条件，或者加大怪物属性！ 来来回回就那9张图！ ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜💙💚💛🧡❤️ 所以就算加了限制条件还是大差不差的玩法，虽然有那么两关确实蛮难的，卡了好久！ 我在一关最久卡了2小时，我的好友们也是7~9小时就全成就了！ 就对比下来，游戏还是比较中规中矩，内容偏少~ 不太对得起这个价格！ 也没有特别吸引人的画风和音效，技能也就大差不差，来来回回就9张图！ 就是感觉可以玩，也不错，但是没有很特色和惊艳我的地方~ 有点像能喝的白开水，可能我还是更喜欢很多添加的可乐吧！ 所以我感觉半价左右入手比较合适！ ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜💙💚💛🧡❤️ 除了价格，还有的建议就是： 希望可以添加一个加速选项，有时候等的真的很急...尤其尤其是最后一个boss打半天，好像加速啊啊啊啊啊啊！（所以才有了“挂机游戏标签”？） 还有希望塔选项的优先级可以高一点，有时候我要点附魔，旁边有小怪啥的，就没点上，有时候就差几秒可能就G了，我那个急性子啊啊啊啊啊啊！ 就是希望在升级附魔的时候，可以不会被选项下面的小怪干扰！ ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜💙💚💛🧡❤️ 最后还是比较开心的能玩到这个游戏！ 也算是及格作品吧！ 最后这个❤的天赋真好看，作者一定是个浪漫的小可爱吧~！ https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3636756518

Aight, hear me out, I know I gave this a THUMBS DOWN but only for reasons that I PERSONALLY can't overlook. This game still has many positives to offer and might even be exactly what you are looking for! Since I still think the game itself is quite ok/good why not start with the good parts! PROS: - Fair Price! Got it in a bundle so it was even cheaper! - Good Background Music. And the sound design and effects are also top-notch. Exactly what one needs to feel immersed in the gameplay. - Very nice use of Minimalism! Even tho the graphics and everything is very minimalist, there are still a lot of animations, shading and touch-ups that just show that someone really cared to make this look and feel good!! - An ok-ish balance between challenge and fun. Some levels and challenges needed a lot of "brute forcing" which diminished the fun a bit over time. Now for the few bad parts. The stuff I sadly cannot overlook and really bugs the hell out of me! CONS: - Has currently the 'Idler' Tag! Nah, nuh uh! In no way, shape or form is there anything Idle in there! This game really requires a lot of active gameplay, so how the actual hell did it get the Idler tag!! - I don't know how to say this but this game plays more like a 'Strategy Puzzle' game than anything else! Like, yes, it looks like a Tower Defense game and has a lot of Tower Defense mechanics.. but on god, this is a Puzzle game! Every level is another Puzzle you need to solve to get to the next level! Early on there might be multiple ways to solve one level but later on and with the challenges on top of it, you literally only have ONE WAY to beat a level!! Would be all cool and dandy if you didn't have so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ options given to you! To figure out what combinations of Upgrades and Towers you need to beat a specific challenges is a nightmare and literally boils down to brute forcing every single combination till you pass! In the end I think I did get my money's worth out of it and I did 100% it, but every time I started it up I felt kinda let down, ngl.. (Edit:) //(I seem to have confused people as to why I'm disappointed that this game has the Idler Tag despite it having absolutely Zero Idle Game Mechanics. I'm sorry, I try to be more detailed this time around: - On SteamDB you can see the Update History, in which it is clearly shown that when the game was put on the Steam Store it was already given the Idler tag by the Publisher, even before any Screenshots were added to the storepage. It was even given the Clicker and Simulation tags, which I'd call a really far stretch. - The games Demo was also put on Itch.io with the Idler tag and those tags are only set by the Publisher. - A Publisher has the ability to contact Steam Support to request the removal of a misleading tag. I can't personally say how effective steam support is in this matter tho. If you want to help with removing incorrect tags, you can do the following: Click the '+' next to all the tags > In the window that opens, hover your mouse over the tag you want to report > A flag should appear which lets you report the selected tag. One could say it was given these tags to reach a wider costomer range, in which case I think it would be a misleading advertisement. Or it could have just been a mistake. But the fact that it's still there is why I took one point away from my total internal review score to be honest. Hope this explains it better now.)// TL;DR Good price, enjoyable to look at, ok-ish gameplay loop, misleading tags!

[h2]This is a weird review[/h2] The game designer in me loves this. The systems are awesome, the resources and how to collect them are great, the aesthetic is minimalistic but polished, the game can be played in quick bursts. The player in me hates this. Grind-style Incremental games are really annoying, as I hate spending thousands to millions of a resource for 0.1% more of some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Grinding and replaying "the same level" with multiple goals is annoying - I'm not a completionist. The above two paragraphs are literally dichotomies. I don't think I've ever ran into a game that equally balanced the scales for me. I would usually find something that I appreciate in both design and play, but for this game, I don't know man. [h1]Other kinda random thoughts[/h1] [list] [*]Despite advertising an "incremental" genre, there's very low content depth [*]I'd put this game at 5$, not 7$ [*]Grind-style Incremental games are not my jam. I prefer Scale-style Incremental. [*]Reached end game in about 3 hours. Fell asleep for 3 hours (during demo, Steam hours is incorrect). [*]I don't know if I'll play it again. [*]I experimented a little bit, and saw 80% of what this game can offer [*]Music is fantastic but only during bosses or endgame. Wish the normal music was awesome too. [*]I'm not a fan of the disorganized skill tree. Made it challenging to track nodes in a macro scale. [*]That said, there was good quality of life features to make it easy to track nodes in a micro scale. [*]The demo made it seem like there was a lot more to the game, only for there to be one more new feature. [/list] But I actually still recommend the game. The designer in me loves the systems and how they interact with each other; though the player in me wishes there was a lot more. I am hoping the devs find a way to appeal to turret defense players more. Mixing genres behind skill-walls can cause players of either genre to lose enjoyment. I immediately felt the incremental part of the game during the demo and wasn't sure if I wanted to buy it. But as I played through the demo, interesting stuff kept getting unlocked and I was sold. Then I bought the game, played like two more levels, and realized there was no more interesting stuff. That felt bad. I've never thought I'd say that I feel scammed from a Demo. I hope to see more content.

I really wanted to leave a positive review, but the game left me with mixed feelings. I like the minimalist art style, but I expected more overall. The game features a large upgrade tree, but there are only about 10 levels, which you have to replay over and over again. You can’t realistically beat levels on your first attempt, so the gameplay loop becomes losing repeatedly just to earn points and upgrade your towers. These constant losses quickly become frustrating, and after about 1.5 hours, I had little desire to return to the game. Ideally, you’re supposed to respec your upgrade tree for each level and rebuild your configuration, but this feels overly complicated and takes away from the sense of progression.

After 100%-ing Outhold and unlocking all 15 achievements legitimately, I can safely say this is one of the most fun games I have personally played. The strongest part of the game is its simplicity. The graphics are not amazing, but they do not need to be. The visual design does its job... every enemy is distinct enough to recognize quickly, and the same applies to the towers. The skill tree is also excellent. Incremental games eventually turn their Skill Trees into mandatory number inflation. You reach a point where you are not really making choices anymore; you are just buying everything. But this skill tree gives you options without making every option mandatory. Some upgrades even come with tradeoffs, like the Coin Cannon, Heavy Arrows, etc. Personally, I never used the Fire Tower or the Coin Cannon, and still did completely fine. Another player could probably do the opposite and also do fine. That kind of flexibility is common in good tower defense games, but it is much harder to balance inside an incremental game. The challenges are another strong point. Prestige is a harder version of the core levels. Token Limit gives you, well, Token Limits to spend. Endless is self explanatory, but it also contains the same system that Token Limit has... the difference is that it has different limits and so on. Token Limit is especially well designed because it complements the skill tree. There are very few “wrong” upgrades as long as you understand your build, the mode pushes you to think about what matters instead of just maxing everything blindly. (Which differs from almost all incremental games). Another point is that this game uses both its tower defense layer and its skill tree layer at the same time, and neither system is less important. That balance is extremely hard, and easy to get out of hand from my understanding. The main problem is the length. It only took me around 6 hours to 100% the game without using guides. Someone who knows exactly what they are doing could probably finish it in around 5 hours, perhaps way faster with predetermined guides. What's left after that is... well, you can go for leaderboard runs, (like I did), but outside of that there is nothing to do. The challenges also are not that hard. I liked them, but most took one or two attempts. I personally understand why the developer may not have wanted to make the game that difficult, given how simple this game is. Still, the game would benefit from a harder game mode. Something like a “Nightmare Mode” could work for example. Maybe a mode where Prestige, Token Limit and Endless all combine. That'd be interesting. Overall, - The skill tree system is excellent. - The gameplay is extremely engaging. - The blend between TD and Incremental games was done right - The Towers are (kinda) balanced. But the game is short, and it never reaches the point where you need to think. 8.5/10, fun, but short.

It's fine if you are looking for deep meaningful improvements that you feel are going to add to a super immersive game then this is not it. If you want an background chill simple TD game then sure. Honestly to many negatives for me to thumbs up sorry. Buy it on sale if you are interested. I got it during the summer sale so I'm not to bitter.

非常推荐的硬核塔防游戏（史低+组合包13.49r入） 优点： ①易上手。塔防种类只有飞箭、闪电、火焰、金币、脉冲5种，怪物种类也只有普通怪、加速怪、盾牌怪、BOSS几种，能否通关全看布局。 ②局外成长可观。前期有多种路径可选，在遇到拿不下的关卡时可以换其他方法；后期可以统统拿下，小孩子才做选择，想怎么打就怎么打。 ③难精通。关卡分为普通、无尽（可选是否代币限制）、声望（难度大幅提升）、代币限制四种，难度层层递进。而且还有全网速度排名，拉高游戏期待。 ④用风、冰、火、土、光五种属性来弥补塔种类不足的问题，不同塔搭配不同属性有不同的效果。以下几种搭配都是很不错的选择：光+脉冲塔，超大范围减速；风+火焰塔，快速叠加燃烧；土+闪电塔，伤害爆表；冰+闪电塔，一步都别想动。 缺点： ①过于硬核。普通前期代币不多、声望/代币限制难度有点高，很容易劝退玩家。 ②关卡数量太少，如果有创意工坊让玩家自己设计，游戏寿命会大幅增加。

I'm a gamedev myself, and that's the only review you need [h1]Short description[/h1][hr][/hr] An incremental tower defense game [h1]Worth highlighting / What is unique[/h1][hr][/hr] - Upgrade types. There are several types, which I liked - Progression upgrades. As you reach certain lifetime currency milestone, you get them for free. These are mostly QOL features - 2 base currency upgrades and 3 unique currencies (one for completing a level, another for completing a level fast, and another for completing a challenge) - Skill building. At the start, you have just 1 tower, and you can unlock new ones with stars (currency earned by finishing a level). So you must choose what to invest in. Or try out different builds. You can reset the whole skill tree at any point. [h1] Overall rating 4/10[/h1][hr][/hr] I really liked the concept, but it lacks content for me I played the demo for 40 min, migrated the save, and finished the main game (including all 10 level challenges and all fast level completions) in under 2 hours. That makes it 2.5 hours total It started becoming repetitive after ~1.5 hours. At this point, your build doesn't matter much, and all levels become very easy and grindy. There is no real challenge or strategy involved. You don't even feel like you're progressing because nothing new is added. Only numbers increase a bit. After finishing the main game, you have some sort of New Game +, so you can finish all levels with different multipliers, so to say, but for me it's not fun So despite a good first impression, a great concept, and decent visuals, I don't think just 1 hour of meaningful gameplay is worth it Not recommended [h1]Extra[/h1][hr][/hr] Follow my curator page, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45084582-Dev-inspiration/] Dev inspiration[/url] for more reviews from a developer's perspective.

I really enjoy simplistic tower defense games such as this one. Outhold is a to-the-point game that uses basic shapes to represent your arsenal (for example lightning towers are represented by triangles). Your skill tree is immediately presented to you, with a few different types of currency that are utilized to improve a multitude of abilities and quality of life aspects. My time with the game was so much fun, up until the 7th stage. The above stage (for me anyways) represented a massive shift in tactics and playstyle. Personally, I enjoy taking my time as I build my defenses and form a strategy based on what's being presented. Stage 7 (specifically at the last wave) is where the slow and cautious such as myself are forced to throw caution into the wind. The attacking party quickly commences a fast-paced and rabid offensive. Slow and steady is no longer an option, as the absolute need to accelerate waves in return for additional funds becomes unavoidable. The game rapidly morphs into a game of speed chess (you know, the one where they slam the timers at the end of their turn). The ability to be proactive shifts in the blink of an eye to the absolute necessity of being fast and reactive. I powered through for an additional 2-3 stages before I had enough. In my opinion, the game had moved away from the traditional tower defense and into a speed-based design. I was in awe of what Tellus Games had accomplished (with so little) through the first 6 stages. It scratched an enduring itch that has not been met in quite a while. Soon after I was disappointed by the abrupt left turn that removed us strategists from the seemingly beautiful equation. Regardless, overall I enjoyed the experience, and look forward to upcoming projects from Tellus Games. FINAL RATING: 6/10
